alternatives.concept: Sociological theory, inequality, collective action and civil society form a sustained foundation, supported by quantitative and qualitative research, econometrics and evidence synthesis. Developmental psychology, social psychology, economics, politics and law add complementary perspectives. UCR has less dedicated family and life-course sociology, survey fieldwork, scale construction and mixed-methods integration, and does not reproduce the required internship or sociology thesis.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two qualified substantial responses retained; each37.5ECsociology plus distinct methods or political/environmental application. No dedicated demography/family/migration sequence or third coherent distinct sociology response can be assembled merely by relabelling adjacent psychology/law. Three is a maximum, not target.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce sociological perspectives on social institutions and relationships.
Both develop sociological questions and ways of interpreting social phenomena.
Both analyse inequality and collective responses; UCR centres movements and environmental justice.
Both develop contemporary sociological theory; UCR includes different theorists and themes.
Both connect culture/media to social difference; UCR centres racial representation.
No single UCR course covers this specific sociology of household decisions at the same scope.
Both address life-course change, with UCR approaching it through developmental psychology.
Related UCR sociology courses examine institutions and individuals but do not duplicate this micro-macro theory component.
Both teach social inquiry, with UCR focused on qualitative methods.
Both cover descriptive statistics for social research, with UCR spanning business and behavioural examples.
Radboud requires a 9-EC supervised survey research project; related UCR methods courses are not that same credited project.
Both teach inferential quantitative analysis of social/behavioural data.
UCR offers philosophy courses but no single scheduled component equivalent to this social-science philosophy requirement.
UCR statistics touch measurement but do not reproduce the specific scale-construction course.
Both teach regression analysis; UCR econometrics uses economic and social datasets.
Radboud requires a second 9-EC collaborative empirical sociology project; UCR coursework is related but not equivalent.
Mixed-methods integration is a distinct required sociology course; systematic review/meta-analysis does not substitute for qualitative and quantitative fieldwork.
The required 9-EC independent sociology thesis is not equivalent to ordinary UCR courses.
Both address institutions and justice surrounding crime; UCR gives a broad legal and social introduction rather than a focused sociology of criminality.
Both examine group relations and social influence; UCR approaches these psychologically.
Both examine how evidence relates to public policy; UCR focuses on public economics.
No closely comparable retained UCR component; public debate and sociological skills remain a distinct requirement.
Both involve academic and personal development in distinct curricular settings.
Professional and personal development remains a distinct Radboud course.
Both examine political contestation and institutional change; UCR focuses on EU politics.
Both engage climate and inequality, but UCR’s course centres climate science and impacts.
This unrestricted 6-EC course is student-selected; no fixed UCR equivalent is imposed.
Third-year Radboud professional development is a separate credited requirement.
Genuine 12-EC free space remains open to student choice.
The compulsory 13-EC labour-market internship has no same credited UCR placement.

notes.text: Both UCR programmes sustain sociology and empirical social inquiry, with complementary psychology, law, economics and political or environmental study. Radboud provides a denser disciplinary sequence in families and life courses, successive supervised survey projects, scale construction and mixed methods, a compulsory 13 EC internship and a 9 EC sociology thesis. Related UCR courses are not degree equivalence or credit-transfer advice.

audience.programmeDescription: Sociology at Radboud studies inequality, social relationships and conflict. It integrates sociological theory, quantitative social research, policy questions, families and life courses through successive empirical projects, an internship and a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Both UCR programmes contain 37.5 EC of sociology courses, including qualitative research. The closest match adds statistics, econometrics, systematic review and developmental perspectives. The second connects sociology to political change, climate communication and sustainability governance. Both offer substantive related study while leaving gaps in dedicated family and life-course sociology, survey projects, scale construction, mixed-method fieldwork and the required internship and thesis.

curriculum.routeLabel: Ordinary bachelor; Political Change and Opposition plus Climate Change and Inequality
curriculum.limitation: The complete 180 EC contains 150 EC of compulsory study, 12 EC of restricted sociology choices and 18 EC of open electives. The two displayed choices are permitted examples; Diversities in Care is an alternative, inseparable 5+1 EC pair. RADAr-NL is mandatory without credit. Second-year entry requires 42 EC of Year 1; compulsory Year 3 requires all of Year 1. Internship entry requires 90 compulsory EC, including all of Year 1 and a pass in Leerproject 2 or Leefstijlen, plus career training before the placement. Methods and thesis progression conditions apply. This annual framework does not guarantee future offerings. UCR does not confer this degree, a professional qualification or automatic master admission.
